# Phase Two — Critique and Twenty-Plus Improvements

The Awtsmoos gives critique the strength of Gevurah, so added light does not become added noise.
Awtsmoos.com should preserve what already works, then remove the weights that obscure the living choice.

## Evidence That Changes Phase One

Phase One suspected that advanced-search disclosure might be unwired. Inspection disproved that suspicion: `form.css` imports `form-disclosure.css`, `SearchApp.boot()` initializes `SearchControlDisclosure`, and the controller moves the existing controls into a native `<details>` element without changing IDs. Therefore search logic should remain intact unless runtime evidence later proves otherwise.

## Improvements To The Original Plan

1. Preserve `SearchControlDisclosure.js`; do not rebuild a behavior already modular and semantically sound.
2. Treat the screenshot’s compact Search Options block as successful progressive disclosure, not the source of the remaining clutter.
3. Focus first on **page hierarchy**, not search-mode semantics.
4. Reduce hero vertical dominance so the query and first result own more of the first viewport.
5. Remove or demote duplicate assurance copy when metadata already proves provenance inside results.
6. Keep one primary visual accent for the search action; do not let every border, badge, tab, and rail card glow equally.
7. Keep scope navigation available but visually subordinate to the search task.
8. Keep result status close to results, but make idle status quiet rather than another boxed panel.
9. Keep query and results in the same dominant column at desktop widths.
10. Reconsider the permanent desktop discovery rail; secondary context should not always consume 17–21rem of width.
11. Prefer one compact context affordance that can reveal lanes/history/help instead of three always-visible cards.
12. On medium widths, do not merely move the entire rail below results as two more large cards; reduce its default presence.
13. On phone widths, do not make secondary context an 86vw horizontal carousel by default; that creates another exploration surface before the user finishes reading results.
14. Preserve the existing safe-area bottom padding and horizontal scope navigation safeguards.
15. Preserve 16px minimum form text, existing focus-visible rings, and native details semantics.
16. Keep loading/error/empty states explicit, but reduce decorative containment around ordinary status text.
17. Keep existing search history behavior and lane discovery data; change prominence, not capability.
18. Do not touch shared Civilization token/base/component styles for a route-local problem.
19. Do not create a new global shell or global override in the first implementation wave.
20. Do not modify dirty screenshot families while other agents are actively changing them.
21. Treat short-height desktop as a separate ergonomic case because the sticky form can otherwise consume disproportionate vertical space.
22. Measure whether the current sticky form collides with shared shell/header height before deciding to retain stickiness.
23. Keep URL/deep-link query state and mode semantics untouched unless runtime testing proves a defect.
24. Preserve exact Hebrew, Tanach, and persisted-library modes while changing only how secondary choices are presented.
25. Preserve result provenance, coordinates, rank/score, and destination links; visual simplification must never erase trust data.
26. Avoid rewriting JS solely to toggle presentational panels when native HTML/CSS can express the same state accessibly.
27. Prefer existing small CSS ownership files over one replacement stylesheet.
28. Add no test files until the first implementation draft exists; then test the actual changed contract.

## Revised Problem Statement

Sefarim is not primarily broken because it lacks progressive disclosure. It is visually overloaded because the route treats identity, assurances, navigation, search controls, result state, lane discovery, local history, and help as simultaneously important. The reconstruction must establish a dominant sequence:

**Where am I? → What am I searching? → What did the library find? → What context do I want next?**

## NEXT_ACTION

Write the improved Phase Two architecture around a search-first content sequence, then make a specific candidate file plan without yet approving production mutation.
